newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinian Airlines starts scheduled flights.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Airlines starts scheduled flights.

text.p: Palestinian Airlines announced on Monday it would launch its first scheduled international flights next month with twice-weekly trips to Jordan.

The airline company, which cannot fly from Palestinian-ruled Gaza until an airport is completed there and Israel gives approval for flights, has been operating charter flights from nearby El-Arish in Egypt.

"This is the first scheduled flight," said Maher Assaf, ticketing officer at Karmel Tourism and Travel Company. He said the first plane, a 42-seater Fokker 15, would leave Amman for El-Arish on June 1.
Palestinian Airlines's first flights were a series of charter flights carrying pilgrims from Gaza between Port Said in Egypt and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.
Gaza was handed over to Palestinian rule under a 1993 PLO-Israeli peace deal. Israel approved the building of a Palestinian airport but it has demanded the facility fall under its security control.
